Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Alyssa Chen (Celestia Head of ML), Marcus Liu (Celestia Platform), Rita Gomez (CTO), Evan Price (Analytics)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): QBR covering March usage and costs, request for pilot for Dedicated capacity, security docs requested, action items listed.
---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, with Samir and Priya. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alyssa: Hi Jordan, good, thanks. Busy quarter, so appreciate the time.
[00:10] Rita: Yup, thanks. We want to focus on cost and reliability, and then roadmap fit for Q2.
[00:16] Jordan: Perfect. We'll kick off with high-level usage and cost trends, Samir will go into latency and reliability details, and Priya will cover the roadmap and next steps.
[00:24] Marcus: Quick ask, can you share the last 90 days token and embedding breakdown up front? That's what the exec team wants.
[00:31] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach the report after this call — Jordan will send.
[00:35] Samir: I'll also drop the latency logs and the tail 95/99 percentile numbers. We saw a small incident last month that we can walk through.
[00:42] Evan: Sounds good.
[00:45] Jordan: Ok, starting with usage: Celestia's overall token consumption is up ~42% q/q, driven largely by customer-facing summarization and a bump in embedding volume for search. Embeddings make up roughly 28% of total spend now.
[01:05] Alyssa: That matches what we saw; search embed calls spiked after the promo. We didn't batch them aggressively because we were worried about freshness.
[01:12] Samir: A couple of places to save: prefix caching for chat flows and batching for embeddings — we have recommendations in Redwood Optimize that could cut cost 15-30% depending on hit rate.
[01:28] Marcus: We turned off prefix caching initially because of some state concerns and multi-tenant issues. Is there a guide for safe cache invalidation patterns?
[01:36] Samir: Yep, we'll share our caching patterns doc. There's an example for per-customer cache keys and TTLs aligned to session lifetime. Also, server-side KV cache can be scoped to VPC in Dedicated.
[01:50] Rita: Security is huge for us — we need SOC 2, SSO, KMS integration, and EU data residency for some PHI-adjacent logs. Can Redwood support that in Dedicated?
[02:02] Jordan: Yes — Dedicated and Private both have KMS/HSM options, and we support SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll send the SOC 2 and security playbook. For EU residency, we can pin region for the Dedicated pool.
[02:15] Alyssa: Great. Any compliance caveats around logging — can we redact PII before logs are stored?
[02:21] Priya: You can configure audit log retention and choose to redact at ingest, or route logs to your own SIEM via the private deployment options. We'll include the guide.
[02:31] Jordan: Moving to reliability — Samir, can you walk us through the incident last month?
[02:36] Samir: Sure. On Feb 11 we observed a burst in long-context requests that inflated KV cache misses; some requests hit a cold path causing tail latency spikes at the 95/99. The root cause was a combination of a large prompt (16k context) and concurrent model swaps during autoscaling which increased queuing.
[02:58] Evan: We saw a few customer complaints about a slow chat response window. It lasted like 8-10 minutes?
[03:03] Samir: Correct. We had queuing and a handful of timeouts. We've since tuned autoscaler thresholds and added backpressure for very long contexts. For a more predictable SLA, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation.
[03:18] Rita: Can you quantify expected latencies on Dedicated vs Hosted for our workload?
[03:23] Samir: Rough numbers: hosted median token latency ~45ms, p95 ~180ms for standard requests; on Dedicated we expect median ~30ms and p95 under 120ms with proper batching and pinned kernels — but we should run benchmarks with your exact prompt mix.
[03:39] Marcus: We do a lot of long-context summarization — 8k-16k tokens. Is the runtime optimized for that? We heard about KV cache improvements but not sure if it's in our stack.
[03:48] Samir: Yes, the runtime has KV cache management and attention optimizations. For 16k we recommend quantization profiles and tuned kernels — again this is something the SE team would validate in a pilot.
[04:01] Alyssa: Cost is the other big thing. If we move to Dedicated, what's the expected unit cost change? We don't want to over-commit and pay for idle GPUs.
[04:10] Jordan: Dedicated shifts capex to a fixed monthly for reserved capacity plus lower per-token variances — in many cases unit cost goes down if you have predictable sustained throughput. We can model a blended cost comparison based on your 90-day usage.
[04:26] Evan: Do you have a spreadsheet model? We've been doing rough math in-house but would like Redwood's numbers.
[04:31] Jordan: Yes — we'll attach a cost model spreadsheet that shows break-even points for different commit levels and burst to hosted.
[04:38] Rita: Another question on fallbacks — if a Dedicated pool has an outage, does Redwood fail over to hosted automatically? We need graceful degradation.
[04:47] Samir: You can configure automatic fallback policies to route to hosted variant or a smaller compatible model. It's part of the routing layer. We'll show the config during the scoping call.
[04:58] Alyssa: On the roadmap side, can we align on features for Q2? Priorities: 1) latency fix for long context, 2) cost rollback from embeddings, 3) SSO + KMS integration checklist.
[05:09] Priya: Noted — we can prioritize a pilot for Dedicated to validate 1 and 2, and security docs for 3.
[05:16] Marcus: Timeline wise, we'd like a pilot in April and a potential rollout in May if the numbers look good. Is that realistic?
[05:22] Jordan: That's realistic. Next steps would be: send the usage report and cost model this week, run a short benchmark (Samir) mid-March, and kick off a Dedicated scoping call the week of March 22.
[05:35] Rita: Ok. For the pilot, can we bring our infra lead into the scoping call? They'll need details on VPC peering and KMS.
[05:43] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include the infra contacts.
[05:46] Alyssa: One more operational ask — can we get token-level cost attribution per route? That helps product team chargeback.
[05:53] Priya: Yes we have the console reports that break down by route, model, and token type. We'll pull a sample export for you.
[06:02] Evan: Any recommended immediate wins we can implement ourselves to reduce cost this quarter?
[06:07] Samir: Short list: enable embedding batching with 500-1k batch sizes where possible, activate prefix caching for chat with per-tenant keys, reduce max tokens for low-value assistants, and enable model selection rules to prefer smaller model variants for non-critical paths.
[06:26] Marcus: About model selection rules — can that be dynamic based on latency? We want to route to cheaper models during peak times.
[06:32] Samir: Yes, routing policies can be set by latency, cost, or region and support automatic fallback. We'll demo that in the scoping session.
[06:40] Rita: Regarding security review, we'll need: SOC 2 report, encryption at rest details, KMS integration steps, and contract language for data residency. Can you consolidate in one packet?
[06:50] Jordan: Yes, Jordan will send the security packet and legal will follow up re: contract addendum for data residency.
[06:56] Alyssa: About the incident — any postmortem or RCA we can review?
[07:01] Samir: We have a short RCA; I'll attach it. High level: autoscaler thresholds + concurrent large requests caused queuing. Mitigation applied.
[07:10] Evan: Good.
[07:13] Jordan: Let's recap action items and owners.
[07:16] Priya: I'll read them out: Jordan to send usage and cost report; Samir to run dedicated benchmark for long context; Alyssa to provide prioritized prompts; Jordan to send security/SOC2 packet; schedule scoping call week of March 22.
[07:29] Alyssa: That sounds right.
[07:32] Rita: Quick question — any ETA on RDW new kernel updates you mentioned last quarter? We heard there was an optimizer landing.
[07:39] Samir: There's a kernel update scheduled in mid-April for better attention kernels; we'll check compat with your model family and include notes in the benchmark.
[07:49] Marcus: Great.
[07:51] Jordan: Ok we're near the top of the hour. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:57] Alyssa: Thanks.
[07:58] Rita: Thanks all.
[08:00] Jordan: End call.
